questions.q: What is the difference between invention and innovation?
options: Invention is the new idea; innovation is bringing it into use
Invention is only done by governments
questions.why: Innovation turns the idea into something used or sold.

questions.q: Match each example to its type.
pairs: A factory installs robots to weld cars
A firm launches a new foldable phone
An engineer draws up a new battery design
questions.why: New ways of making things, new things to sell, and the original idea.

questions.q: New technology lowers a firm's costs. What is the likely effect on its market?
questions.why: Lower costs mean more is supplied at every price.

options: New technology and firms replacing old ones
questions.why: It is the process Schumpeter described.

questions.q: Technological change can make a market more competitive or less competitive.
questions.why: It can lower barriers to entry or help a few firms dominate.

questions.q: Which of these shows technology raising competition?
options: A patent protects one firm's design
Small sellers can reach customers worldwide online
questions.why: Selling online lowers barriers to entry.

questions.q: Explain one benefit and one cost of creative destruction.

ideas.label: Benefit: new, better or cheaper products, higher productivity or growth
Cost: old firms close or workers lose jobs

questions.model: Consumers gain new and cheaper products, and productivity rises. But old firms close and their workers can lose their jobs, at least in the short run.
questions.why: One gain and one loss are needed.

tests.answer: Consumers get new products but workers in old firms lose their jobs.
